solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: See what?

parts.note: an invitation to look at something, phrased as the old-fashioned command to look and wonder

explanation.surface: A puzzled request to be shown something.
explanation.walkthrough: The blogger treats this as a cryptic definition. Commenters suspected 'what' was printed in bold, giving EH inside BOLD, but that formatting did not survive publication.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic imperative 'lo, look!' is exactly what someone says when bidding another to see what is there.

clue.text: Bag second set of suits

parts.note: to second a proposal is to back it
a pack of cards contains the four suits

explanation.surface: Obtain a second set of clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suits' suggests clothes but means the card suits.
explanation.definitionFit: A backpack is a bag carried on the back with straps over the shoulders.

clue.text: After stripping off, choose gowns not originally needed in US prisons

indicators.note: stripping off removes the outer letters of the word choose, keeping its core
not here means without, so a letter is taken out of the word gowns
originally points to the opening letter of the word needed

explanation.surface: Someone choosing what to wear in American jails finds gowns unnecessary.
explanation.walkthrough: The N removed comes from 'needed', not from 'not'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoosegow is American slang for a jail, from Spanish juzgado, so the plural names US prisons.

clue.text: Off-duty senior cabinet member seen in toilet in cricket ground, having drunk ale

indicators.note: the toilet is seen in, that is placed within, the name of the ground

parts.note: Lord's is the famous cricket ground in London
a privy is an outdoor toilet

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters of the word ale are knocked about

explanation.surface: A minister off duty is spotted in the toilets at a cricket ground after a few beers.
explanation.walkthrough: LORD'S is a London cricket ground. 'Off-duty' is part of the definition: the Lord Privy Seal is a senior British government post with no set duties.
explanation.definitionFit: This ancient ministerial office sits in the British cabinet but carries no departmental responsibilities, hence off-duty.

clue.text: Dislocate a girl's shoulder, say

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, so 'a girl's' gives DI'S
the shoulder is an example of a joint in the body

explanation.surface: Someone dislocates a young woman's shoulder, perhaps in an accident.
explanation.definitionFit: To dislocate a bone is to put it out of its socket, separating the parts that fit together.

clue.text: Remaining with top off when putting bun in the oven

indicators.note: off suggests the letters of the two words are wrong or awry, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone bakes topless, leaving the top off while putting a bun in the oven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting a bun in the oven' is British slang for getting someone pregnant.
explanation.definitionFit: Impregnation is making someone pregnant, which the slang idiom about baking describes.

clue.text: Only drama, no sex? Please yourself!

parts.note: only and just both mean merely

indicators.note: no means the play's title is left without the word for sex appeal

parts.note: As You Like It is a Shakespeare comedy
it is slang for sex or sex appeal

explanation.surface: Someone wants a drama with no sex in it, and is told to suit themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' is old slang for sex appeal, so 'no sex' drops IT from the end of the play's title.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase tells someone to do whatever pleases them, the same idiom as suit yourself.

clue.text: Current number bedded or embedded

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current
laid, in the slang sense of having had sex with, means bedded

explanation.surface: A tally of who has been bedded, now or before.
explanation.definitionFit: Inlaid describes decoration set into a surface, so it means fixed or embedded within it.

clue.text: Struggle if lust's uncontrolled? To a point

indicators.note: uncontrolled tells us the letters of lust's run wild into a new order

parts.note: E, east, is one of the points of the compass

explanation.surface: A fight that breaks out when desire gets out of hand, up to a point.
explanation.definitionFit: A tussle is a vigorous scuffle or contest, a physical struggle.

clue.text: Singers collectively are rarely so rich

indicators.note: read as 'in a rare, unusual fashion', telling us to arrange the letters of the words so rich unusually

explanation.surface: A wry observation that singers as a group are seldom wealthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rarely' looks like part of the claim about money but is the anagram signal for SO RICH.
explanation.definitionFit: Choirs are organised groups of singers performing together, so the plural names singers taken as bodies.

clue.text: During affairs, initially the French letters hide John Thomas and the like

indicators.note: initially tells us to take only the opening letter of the word affairs
the word posts is said to hide, or conceal, the French article inside it

parts.note: letters sent by mail are posts
le is the French masculine form of 'the'

explanation.surface: A risqué image of French letters (condoms) and John Thomas (slang for penis) during affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface leans on British slang: 'French letters' are condoms and 'John Thomas' is the penis. Here John and Thomas are two of Jesus's disciples.
explanation.definitionFit: John and Thomas were two of the twelve disciples sent out by Jesus, so they and their fellows are examples.

clue.text: Linguistic specialists corrected slight lisp, with two separate intakes of oxygen

indicators.note: corrected suggests the words slight lisp are put right by rearranging

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen, taken in twice

explanation.surface: Speech therapists fixed a lisp while the patient took two deep breaths.
explanation.walkthrough: The two O's go in separately, after the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Philologists study the history and structure of languages, so they are experts in language.

clue.text: Telegraph given endless grief, reworking former Sun feature

indicators.note: reworking signals the letters of the newspaper name and the shortened word are rearranged
endless means the word grief loses its final letter

explanation.surface: One newspaper, the Telegraph, troubled by remaking a feature of a rival, the Sun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the last letter of 'grief' to give GRIE; 'reworking' rearranges TELEGRAPH plus GRIE. The Sun is a British tabloid; for decades its third page showed a topless model.
explanation.definitionFit: The topless model on the tabloid's third page was a long-running regular item of that newspaper until it was dropped.

clue.text: See 12
See 12

What actors learn, getting sucked into playwright's lack of courage

indicators.note: the actors' text is drawn inside the possessive playwright's name

parts.note: Noel Coward was an English playwright, so 'playwright's' gives COWARD'S
actors memorise their lines from the script

explanation.surface: Actors learning their parts are drawn into a dramatist's timidity.
explanation.walkthrough: Noel Coward was a famous English playwright and actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cowardly is the opposite of bravery, so the abstract noun for it is a want of courage.

clue.text: Plurality of bone marrow, essentially

parts.note: the heart of the word marrow is a pair of letter R, and R is short for radius, so two of them make plural ones

explanation.surface: Bone marrow at its essence is being described.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle of 'marrow' is RR, read as two R's, R being an abbreviation for radius.
explanation.definitionFit: The radius is a forearm bone; its regular plural form names more than one of them.

clue.text: Scatty about taking exercise? An actor might be

indicators.note: taking means the rearranged letters take in the exercise abbreviation
about suggests the letters of Scatty are turned around into a new order

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school exercise

explanation.surface: Someone scatterbrained about doing exercise, and an actor might be so too.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors repeatedly given the same kind of part are said to be stuck in one role type.

clue.text: Showing gradual development, redhead's away

indicators.note: the head, or first letter, of the word for a radical is taken away

parts.note: a red is a political radical, a revolutionary

explanation.surface: Someone with red hair has left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redhead's away' reads as one person leaving, but splits into 'red' (a revolutionary) whose 'head' is 'away'.
explanation.definitionFit: Evolution is change by slow stages, so something evolutionary displays development over time rather than sudden change.

clue.text: Make a contribution after Polish scorer gets rid of clean sheet for Italy

indicators.note: gets rid of the zero, putting the Italy letter in its place

parts.note: Chopin was a Polish composer, one who writes scores
a clean sheet in football means conceding nil, O
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A Polish goalscorer helps out after Italy fails to keep a clean sheet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scorer' suggests football but means a composer of musical scores.
explanation.definitionFit: To chip in is an idiom for contributing, whether money to a collection or a remark.

clue.text: Rings about barman detailed as cook for too long

indicators.note: the rings go about, or around, the shortened name

parts.note: two rings are two letter O shapes

indicators.note: detailed means the composer's name loses its tail, its last letter

parts.note: Verdi, a composer, is a man of musical bars

explanation.surface: A barman is described as a cook surrounded by rings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barman' suggests a pub but is a man of musical bars, the composer Verdi.
explanation.definitionFit: Overdoing food means cooking it past the right point, leaving it for too long on the heat.

clue.text: Own advanced GT? Enjoy oneself!

parts.note: to own something is to have it
A is an abbreviation for advanced, as in A level
G is short for good and T for ..., so the pair of letters stands for those two words

explanation.surface: Owning a fast GT sports car, the advice is to enjoy it.
explanation.walkthrough: GT here is not a car badge: read the letters as abbreviations, G for good and T for time.
explanation.definitionFit: The familiar parting wish to someone setting out on an outing is a way of telling them to enjoy themselves.

clue.text: See 23
See 23
See 3
See 6
Contrary dirty old man, Irish

parts.note: a perv is slang for a lecherous man
Erse is the Irish Gaelic language

explanation.surface: An awkward Irish lecher is being described.
explanation.definitionFit: Perverse means deliberately unreasonable or obstinately opposed, which is what a contrary person is.

clue.text: Car that is fast, going round about

indicators.note: the shuffled word is placed about, or around, the Latin abbreviation
going round suggests the letters of the word fast spin into a new order

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of the Latin for 'that is'

explanation.surface: A speedy car circling around a track.
explanation.definitionFit: The Fiesta is a long-running small car model made by the Ford motor company.

clue.text: Abnormal growth of one new sort of TV curtailed

indicators.note: new tells us to make the letters of the word one into a fresh order
curtailed means the type of television loses its last letter

parts.note: a plasma screen is a type of television

explanation.surface: Something odd growing on a television set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' looks like a description of the TV but rearranges ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A neoplasm is the medical term for a tumour, a mass of tissue growing in an uncontrolled way.

clue.text: Guy takes time providing drinks service

parts.note: to guy someone is to make fun of them, to tease

explanation.surface: A man takes time to provide drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' looks like a man but is the verb meaning to mock.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea set is the cups, saucers and pot used to serve tea, a service for drinks.
